exact_quote: All instructions have an optional guard predicate which controls conditional execution of the instruction. The syntax to specify conditional execution is to prefix an instruction with @{!}p, where p is a predicate variable, optionally negated. Instructions without a guard predicate are executed unconditionally.
context_before: 7541-7546: predicate registers are virtual and have .pred as the type specifier; declaration .reg .pred p, q, r;
context_after: 7551-7552: Predicates are most commonly set as the result of a comparison performed by the setp instruction.
reason_for_inclusion: Primary normative guard rule for BLOCK-2: the guard predicate 'controls conditional execution of the instruction' and instructions without a guard are 'executed unconditionally'. This is the closest official statement connecting the complete guard expression to whether execution occurs; it does not explicitly state the machine-state effect when the guard evaluates false.
